title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support for inclusive territorial governance in the Southern Altiplano as part of the energy transition (360º approach) in Bolivia

description.narrative: On the inclusive territorial governance in the Southern Altiplano, The action responds to the need to ensure that the Southern Altiplano¿s growing strategic importance does not lead to extractive dynamics disconnected from social cohesion, environmental sustainability and democratic legitimacy. Instead, it will strengthen the capacity of public institutions, communities and local stakeholders to plan, manage and shape development pathways linked to critical raw materials, renewable energy, tourism, education, decent work and sustainable value chains. In doing so, it is aligned with EU priorities on Global Gateway, the just green transition, critical raw materials and trusted international partnerships. Its overall objective is to promote inclusive, sustainable and gender-responsive territorial development in Bolivia¿s Southern Altiplano through a Global Gateway 360-degree approach. The action combines improved territorial governance, enhanced access to services, decent employment opportunities and stronger prevention of and response to gender-based violence, while safeguarding fragile ecosystems and supporting a green and just transition. The action is built around four connected pillars. It will strengthen participatory and socially inclusive territorial planning and governance through better planning instruments, digital management tools and dialogue between stakeholders. It will also improve access to technical and vocational training and support entry into the labour market, particularly for women and young people, using a learning-by-doing model based on Territorial Workshop Schools in Uyuni and Potosí. In addition, it will help territorial actors identify and promote sustainable investment opportunities through public-private dialogue, project pipeline development and links with other financing instruments. At the same time, it will strengthen systems to prevent and respond to gender-based violence by consolidating 20 existing local networks and creating 5 new territorial networks in mining municipalities.The action will work closely with complementary Team Europe and Global Gateway initiatives, including COFIDES-managed programmes to improve access to finance for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, decentralised renewable energy solutions for underserved areas, and water and sanitation interventions in the Salars area supported by AECID (contributing with EUR 1M, the IDB and the World Bank Group. These links are intended to connect planning, skills, investment and protection within one coherent territorial results chain.Overall, the initiative is expected to deliver economic, social, environmental and institutional results. It should create decent jobs, strengthen enterprises and make local value chains more resilient. It should also reduce gender-based violence, improve local protection systems and increase the participation of women, young people and Indigenous communities in territorial decision-making. Environmentally, it aims to promote climate-resilient planning, sustainable natural resource management and biodiversity protection. Institutionally, it will reinforce the EU¿s role as a reliable partner for a just transition in territories affected by critical raw materials extraction. In essence, the initiative reflects the Global Gateway¿s 360-degree approach by going beyond infrastructure and investment alone. It combines economic opportunity, gender equality, environmental protection and finance within a conflict-sensitive territorial strategy, offering a holistic response to extractive pressures, migration and inequality.
